scope: Fully dimensioned static canopy, frame, four suspension ropes and harness ring. Deployment and safe human use are outside this display specification.
gaps: Historical suspension lengths, cloth density, joint construction and frame cross sections unknown and assumed.
No deployment simulation or structural certification.
Holder-specific image licence terms not verified.

assumptions.statement: For the displayed aerodynamic comparison use100kg total suspended mass,49m2 projected area, rho1.225kg/m3, g9.81m/s2 and Cd1.2. Cd0.8and1.6 are sensitivity bounds. A second165kg scenario is80kg assumed pilot plus85kg reported replica. Mass is an explicit aerodynamic scenario, not inferred from the geometric mesh.
assumptions.reason: No measured drag coefficient or structural mass breakdown for this exact geometry was located.

assumptions.statement: Static documentary placement at the origin. No inferred motion.
assumptions.reason: Prevents an unfinished study appearing to be a working mechanism.

assumptions.statement: Every numeric dimension, coordinate, orientation, mesh subdivision, tube radius and repeated-element placement in parts is an explicit modern modelling choice except quantities explicitly identified as Leonardo dimensions in the part notes. These values are the complete procedural definition.
assumptions.reason: The folio does not specify fabrication geometry. The model is newly specified from the sheet and never copied from a replica.

assumptions.statement: Every motion limit, pivot, period and rate below is a modern demonstration assumption unless a source is named. All fixed children follow their parent rigidly.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating rate is measured.

animation_notes: No undocumented flight, lift, bounce, mechanism or invisible reset.
Static suspended study. Do not animate a drop as safe, or invisibly reset the canopy.
Keep the base open. Four equilateral7m cloth panels produce a different pyramid height and must not replace the12by12braccia geometry.

sources.title: The Invention of the Parachute

sources.limitations: Publisher bibliography inspected. Full chapter unavailable. Earlier Italian drawings supported separately by CSPA.

sources.title: History of Parachuting and CSPA
sources.supports: Institutional history reports anonymous Italian parachute drawings dated about 1470, earlier than Leonardo.

sources.title: The Notebooks of Leonardo da Vinci, section 1126 footnote
sources.supports: Section 1126 footnote identifies a parachute sketch and refers readers to Saggio plate XVI and Hermann Grothe 1874 page 50.
sources.limitations: This is a cross-reference footnote, not the folio transcription giving 12 braccia dimensions. It establishes located publication references, not historical priority.

sheet_vs_reconstruction: Sheet gives a person beneath a sealed-linen pyramidal canopy and a 12 braccia dimension statement [s-folio].
Soldatini and Somenzi 1952 to 1953 supplied the detailed wooden model frame, cotton cover and dummy [s-model].

Nicholas 2000 used a heavy version and finished under a conventional reserve. Vietti-Teppa 2008 landed with modern fabric, four equilateral 7 m sides and a mesh base without the rigid frame [s-nicholas,s-vietti].
The commissioned model uses the literal square-base and vertical-height reading, never replica photographs [a-geometry].

dimensions.quote: che sia 12 braccia per faccia e alto 12
dimensions.richter_note: Richter 1883 section 1126 footnote mentions a parachute sketch and references Saggio plate XVI and Grothe 1874 page 50. The 12 braccia wording is verified directly on CA1058v in e-Leo, not assigned to the body of Richter section 1126 [s-richter,s-folio].
dimensions.conversion: 12x 0.5836=7.0032 m side and vertical height. The quoted material is pannolino intasato, sealed linen [s-folio].

claims.claimed: A man under this canopy could descend from any great height without injury [s-folio].
claims.tested: The inspected note is a proposal, not a dated test result [s-folio].
claims.built_lifetime: No documented lifetime build or jump located.
claims.later: Nicholas 2000 airborne descent followed by reserve landing. Vietti-Teppa 26 April 2008 direct landing at Payerne after 650 m helicopter exit. Reports distinguish 80 kg versus 85 kg for Nicholas apparatus. Neither is an instrumented test of this precise cloth/structure model [s-vietti,s-85kg].

physics.inputs: A 49 m 2 is the rounded 7x 7 m projected opening, not the sum of four cloth triangles. All other inputs are explicit a-physics assumptions except the reported 85 kg replica mass.
physics.results: 100 kg,Cd 1.2 gives 5.219 m/s. Cd 0.8 gives 6.392 m/s andCd 1.6 gives 4.520 m/s.165 kg,Cd 1.2 gives 6.704 m/s. Equivalent free-fall heights v^2/(2g) are 1.39 m and 2.29 m for 100 and 165 kg. A seven-metre equilateral-face pyramid has vertical height 7/sqrt(2)=4.95 m, unlike Leonardo 12 braccia vertical reading.
physics.limitations: Terminal descent only. Excludes opening shock, oscillation, ground wind, fabric permeability and impact injury. Cd is deliberately assumed, not a measured Leonardo coefficient.
physics.verdict_en: A 7 by 7 m canopy at 100 kg gives about 5.2 m/s in this assumed drag model.
physics.verdict_de: Eine 7 mal 7 m große Kappe sinkt bei 100 kg in diesem angenommenen Widerstandsmodell mit etwa 5,2 m/s.

myths.claim: Leonardo invented the parachute and the 2000 replica landed intact.
myths.earliest_located: The earliest explicit first-parachute attribution actually located here is the contemporary Servimedia 28 June 2000 report. It is not claimed to be the historical first such attribution [s-85kg].
myths.correction: The CSPA history reports earlier Italian drawings about 1470. AFP distinguishes Nicholas reserve landing from Vietti-Teppa modern canopy landing [s-history,s-vietti].

research.confidence: High folio and 12 braccia text. Medium date and test narrative. Low assumed Cd and mass. No safety claim.

geometry_validation.method: Local primitive and mesh geometry transformed through the specified joint hierarchy. Forty-nine poses across 12 seconds, or one static pose. Tube centreline bounds conservatively expanded by radius. Analytic motion extrema and attachment clearances are given in animation_notes.
geometry_validation.result: All tested swept points are inside the declared conservative bounding box. Geometry defines a C exhibit interpretation, not structural certification.

research.publication_cross_reference: Richter 1883, section 1126 footnote, supplies a located reference to Hermann Grothe, Leonardo da Vinci als Ingenieur, Berlin 1874, page 50, and Saggio plate XVI. Those referenced pages were not independently inspected. This is not evidence that either publication first circulated the sketch [s-richter].
